summary: We are testing whether assigning each item type its own placement heuristic (per-type method, 5 options) and co-evolving these assignments alongside type orderings can push the 2D knapsack packer score from ~89 to above 95. This builds on two prior iterations that established MaxRects with multi-ordering search as a solid baseline (89.02).
key_points: Main arm (h-main): Replaces solution.cpp with a v20 packer featuring per-type method assignment (BSSF/BAF/BL/CP/BLSF), co-evolutionary random search over 5^M method vectors × M! orderings, local search over both dimensions, gap-fill post-processing, and 10 deterministic seed orderings. Prediction: score ≥ 95.0 (probed at 95.73).

Negative control (h-control-negative): Runs the current iter-2 solution (uniform method per packing, no per-type differentiation). Prediction: score ≈ 89, confirming the ~6-point gain comes from the MPT mechanism rather than test-set variance.

Confirmation criteria: If main arm scores ≥ 95 AND control scores ≤ 91, the per-type method hypothesis is confirmed. If control also scores ≥ 95, the gain is attributable to test-set changes. If main arm scores < 92, the co-evolutionary overhead or search-space explosion is hurting more than the added flexibility helps.

Key risk: The 5^M method space (up to 5^12 ≈ 244M combinations) combined with M! orderings may be too large for the 1-second time budget; diagnostics include checking for TLE and reducing methods to 3 if needed.
Time/resource budget is carefully partitioned: ~840ms for random search, ~220ms for local search, ~50ms for gap-fill, with a 500-rect cap to prevent quadratic blowup.
